title: A fixed two-argument cheol realization and a nominal-head rival on retained complete contexts
phase: Informed exploratory manual construction. All examples were previously exposed; no independent prediction, new census, model score or reserve test.
question: Can the local daldy dalor cheol construction extend with one unchanged relation and role system, and what changes if cheol instead denotes a nominal relation-bearing entity?

UG1.core: The same unassigned binary C_cheol(x,y) and DY/OR argument roles are held fixed. No concrete verb or physical event is assigned.
UG1.surface_rule: Exactly two immediately preceding complete raw groups, within own-reader paragraph scope and without uncertain gaps/drawing interruption, supply the arguments. First: bare nominal with default DY role, or explicit Bdy with nonempty B. Second: exact Bor with nonempty B. cheol consumes those two arguments once and closes the relation; later words are outside it.
UG1.type_conditions: Bare means not already a recognized conflicting role form. Free or/dy/daiin markers and cheol itself are not silently turned into bare nominal arguments. All nominal content types are hypotheses.
new_costs: New proposed ot+or and qo+or analyses
The paragraph-first fchokshy is now an argument, not a consumed C1 topic
UG1.scope_precision: This is a specific whole-group surface realization; it does not automatically implement every free-marker nominal phrase allowed by older N1/U. Allowing explicit free markers would not fix the decisive y, she or qkol predecessor, where the required OR marker is absent.
UG1.manual_outcome: The three motivating examples are conditionally attachable. Three other already retained examples fail the mandatory OR-second-argument condition. A broader run cannot make this universal contract true.
UG1.decision: Do not use UG1 as the general cheol reader. Its possible local pattern remains a hypothesis; the three fits are chiefly the selected suffix pattern, not evidence of a shared meaning. No per-occurrence role change, silent omitted argument, rightward rescue or new valency is supplied.

manual_panel.UG1_account: y is not B+or; oky lies before the same-paragraph line wrap
qkol is not B+or; first daiin is also not an ordinary unmarked nominal under the marker inventory

H.core: Every exact cheol has the same unassigned nominal description C(z). It denotes a possible nominal relation-bearing node, not a chosen substance, a verb translation or an asserted new physical object. Different occurrences need not refer to the same or different individual.
H.licensed_modifiers: In this bounded application daldy and dalor preserve nominal D; otor and qoor conditionally license OT and QO plus OR. Those inner analyses are new hypotheses. No qkol/qoor substitution, y stripping, reader joining or universal suffix parser is licensed.
H.prefix_scope: Attach the maximal immediately preceding contiguous run of licensed DY-/OR-marked nominal expressions to the cheol head. Each contributes its nominal description and Role_s(z)=x_B. An unmarked or unlicensed group stops the run; do not skip it or give it an implicit DY role. Zero modifiers are allowed. Stay within own-reader paragraph scope. Clear within-paragraph line wraps may continue the run; uncertain seams or drawing interruptions leave attachment unresolved and do not license crossing.
H.functional_specialization: Role_s(g)=d is a single-valued slot relation, explicitly specializing the general nominal-modifier idea to the existing U model. Same role with two values would constrain those values equal; different roles may share a value. This functionality is a model assumption, not a manuscript result.
H.same_marker_content: The fixed contribution of a licensed bound or free s remains Role_s(governor)=dependent. Prefix attachment supplies the written cheol head as governor. A postfix marker keeps its outer governor pending until a separately declared construction binds it to written text; it is not already resolved. Lexical marker content is not separately changed at each occurrence.
H.what_is_outside: Unmarked fchokshy and ckhey remain outside their H phrases. she, y and qkol do not become modifiers merely because they precede cheol. The following bare dal onf45r is not a third inner argument.
H.identity_limits: z and modifier referents are binding variables, not a count of actual objects. No z!=x, x!=y, shared subject or physical event follows. The modifier descriptions and head class remain untranslated.
H.why_not_a_winner: The optional-modifier nominal rule has fewer compulsory arguments than UG1. Allowing bare C accounts for type compatibility, not the surrounding unread text or a historically preferred interpretation.

H_post_U.input: The completed H nominal description with referent z can feed the already declared U marker operation.
H_post_U.rule: A contiguous immediately following run of licensed free markers adds Role_s(e_outer)=z for every marker in that run. All markers in this run retain the same z and outer-governor placeholder. Stop at any other group; no skipping. Stay within own-reader paragraph scope; a clear line wrap may continue the run, but an uncertain seam or drawing interruption does not license crossing.
H_post_U.shared_semantics: Prefix and postfix uses share Role_s(governor)=dependent. Prefix modifiers use z as their governor; postfix markers use z as dependent of the separate outer frame. C must therefore be allowed to act both as a nominal head with slots and as an argument. This is an explicit new type assumption.
H_post_U.f24r1: cheol daiin or => C(z) & Role_daiin(e_outer)=z & Role_or(e_outer)=z. The next line starts qotaiin, not another marker; it is not assigned as the governor here.
H_post_U.f102v1_13: cheol daiin => C(z) & Role_daiin(e_outer)=z. Following qokar remains outside the marked nominal expression and is not silently declared its governor.
H_post_U.f24r18: cheol chol daiin does NOT allow daiin to skip chol and modify cheol. This right-side continuation remains unread under the present H/U licenses.
H_post_U.unbound_obligations: e_outer is a pending written-governor binding, not an invented event. It is not silently equated with z or a prefix-modifier governor. No state change, execution, amount or result follows.
H_post_U.comparison_to_UG: UG1 returns an assertion rather than a nominal input. Feeding that assertion to U would require a new nominalization rule; another sentence segmentation or another daiin function is also possible. Conditional type compatibility does not select H or the marker reading.

f45r_complete_application.scope: All32 exact raw groups remain in original order. The same11 positions receive conditional type/role assignments as U-G;21 remain uninterpreted. No extra coverage or translated-word count is claimed.
f45r_complete_application.bare_dal_obligation: The following bare dal does not by shared spelling choose between the two prior D-description occurrences, identify either with z, or introduce a provably fresh individual. No anaphoric result or last-mentioned-participant default is inserted.

reification_limit: For the two-modifier case one could define C_UG(x,y) iff there exists z [C_H(z) AND Role_dy(z)=x AND Role_or(z)=y]. Without a separately fixed later use of z, relation assertion and nominal relation-bearer may encode the same situation. The noun-vs-assertion type difference is not by itself a semantic discriminator, especially if UG later supplies an explicit nominalization.
reader_sensitivity: f45r.10 daldy dalor cheol and f102v1.24 ckhey qoor cheol are exact in all three readings; paragraph-final status of the latter is marked only byIT/ZL.
IT f21r.8 has fchokshy otor cheol. RF has fchokshy otor sheol; ZL fcho~kshy otor sheol. Do not pool target carrier or initial group count.
IT f24r.18 has standalone y cheol; ZL/RF have whole ycheol. No silent prefix deletion or target admission in those readers.
f24r.18 has two available left groups across the clear within-paragraph line wrap: oky / y. UG1 fails the OR condition, not merely the number of preceding groups.
All actual raw annotations and flags remain in snapshots; alternative readings are not independent manuscript observations.

profiles_and_predecessors.new_role_forms: otor33/38/29, qoor6/5/5, ckhey20/25/24, fchokshy0/1/1 profiles were retrieved separately. Labels, repetitions and reader splits remain; ot/qo nominal stems are not established.
profiles_and_predecessors.prior_semantics: 804/805/806 already investigated material, property and process rivals and selected no cheol meaning.804s f88r.10 content licence concerns cheos, not cheol. No old heat/dry/material gloss is inherited.
profiles_and_predecessors.old_failures: B2/B3, C1 selection limits, N2,1047 and the originalUG local scope remain unchanged. This does not rerun those rules or declare every cheol predicate impossible.
profiles_and_predecessors.nominal_family_obligation: H presently types exact cheol only. It does not invent unrelated meanings for chol/sheol or claim to have explained the L-family variation. Their relation is an unresolved obligation, not a hidden synonym or prefix-normalization rule.

decision: Retain the manual UG1 mismatch and the separately authored H nominal construction with its explicit U continuation. No winner, full reading or lexical meaning is selected. Do not continue a broad UG1 fit or prefer H merely because optional modifiers allow more positions.
next_work: Bind the still-open outer relation after the already written cheol daiin sequences, keeping one typed rule and actual written heads; qotaiin afterf24r.1 and qokar afterf102v1.13 are unassigned candidates to inspect, not assigned governors. Preserve no-skipping and the possibility of separate statements. No further grammatical permissiveness alone is a meaning result.
validation: Bounded independent source and semantic reviews supplied the panel, cross-reader differences, UG1 condition and H/type/reification limits. Root applied one rule per model to every retained target, without a new corpus census, model program or statistical score. Final serialized semantic review by closure_error_audit confirmed the functional specialization and requested explicit unresolved-governor wording and boundary guards; both are included. Final source audit by cross_reading_opportunity matched all20 selected snapshots,12 source digests and6 target IDs; f24r.17-18 clear within-paragraph wrap and cross-reader differences were checked. Source fidelity does not validate semantics.
